articles.headline: Notice (Box No. 430)
articles.summary: Our Correspondents and Subscribers will please take notice that all letters, or anything sent by mail, must be directed to Box No. 430, Philadelphia, Pa.

articles.headline: To Our Friends (editorial)
articles.summary: We have been much gratified by the numerous letters from friends, expressing their pleasure with the appearance and character of our paper. A letter from Bishop Nazrey we publish in another column.

articles.headline: Our City Carriers (notice)
articles.summary: James Wiggins and W. T. Jones are our city carriers, and hope that all who subscribe by the week will always have their money ready for them... All our ministers throughout the connexion are agents for this paper.

articles.headline: Publication Society of Philadelphia (notice)
articles.summary: This Society was organized some years ago to assist in publishing a paper. Mrs. Laws, I believe, is the President... The Young Ladies and Gentlemen in favor of our undertaking [are requested] to meet at our house, No. 619 Pine street, on Monday evening, the 21st inst., to organize themselves into a society to aid in establishing our paper. --Ed.
people: president, Publication Society of Philadelphia (as reported)

articles.headline: Book Depository of the African M. E. Church (advertisement)
articles.summary: Book Depository of the African M. E. Church, No. 619 Pine street, Philadelphia. We keep on hand Sabbath school books, Question Books, Catechisms, and books generally used in the Public Schools; also stationery. [Recurring house notice; captured once here.]

articles.headline: Quarterly Meetings (notice)
articles.summary: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's Quarterly Meeting [next Sabbath]... Rev. Peter Gardiner's Quarterly Meeting will be held at Woodbury, Gloucester co., N. J., Saturday and Sabbath day, the 19th and 20th. [Item on Rev. J. M. Brown and the Repository follows.]

articles.headline: Our First Visit to Bristol (with list of Bristol and Burlington subscribers)
articles.summary: We spent last Sunday at Bristol with our Rev. and esteemed father, Robertson. It was his quarterly meeting. We had a good time together... We sold fifty copies, which were all we had with us, and got some twenty subscribers... We will give the names of those who subscribed for our paper in Bristol.

articles.headline: News from the Churches (mission church; Frankford)
articles.summary: We omitted, in our first issue, the [mention of the] mission [church] in this city. It was not designedly done... Rev. Stephen Smith is the pastor of the mission. They have had a protracted meeting in the mission, which seems to have resulted in good... On Wednesday night we had a meeting at Frankford with father Robertson... the Rev. H. Davis, a local preacher, and his son, take one hundred copies per week to supply Frankford. That is the way to do business. [Also notes a letter from Rev. ... W. Weyman of Frederick, Md.]

articles.headline: The Egyptian [Obelisk] in the Court of St. Peter's
articles.author: Jonathan C. Gibbs
articles.summary: Whenever objects of nature or art have been consecrated by the memory of human affections... Such is the case with the Egyptian Obelisk in the court of St. Peter's. [Signed: Jonathan C. Gibbs, Pastor Seventh St. Presbyterian Church.]

articles.headline: The Arts and Sciences (no. 1)
articles.summary: When we take a retrospective view of the arts and sciences... Now, we colored people have the advantage of the ancients, apprentices, journeymen, and business men... [Unsigned first installment; series continues 26 Jan and 2 Feb.]

articles.headline: A. M. E. Preachers' Association
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: Bro. Weaver:--You have requested me to write an article for our paper... The proper thinking part of the ministry of the Philadelphia district have seen, for a long time, the necessity of an organization of this kind. While our highly esteemed brother, J. P. Campbell, was in our city as general book steward, he, with others, attempted to meet weekly...

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor,--After an absence of over four years from our numerous friends in the east, permit me to speak to them on subjects of importance through your columns... I have for the last four years been travelling through the Western region and the Canadas...

articles.headline: Letter from Brother Brown
articles.author: John M. Brown
articles.summary: Baltimore, Jan. 14th, 1861. Brother Weaver:--I thank you for proving that we can do something, as well as others... Philadelphia alone ought to give you two thousand subscribers. P.S. Your old friend, the Repository, is now out. It contains a fine likeness of the venerable founder of the A. M. E. Church, the late Bishop Allen. Our subscribers in Philadelphia can get them at your book store, No. 619 Pine Street.

articles.headline: Married (Stokes--Robinson?)
articles.summary: On the 3d inst., we had the pleasure of joining in the connubial knot our friends Mr. William Sto[k]es and Miss Anna Ro[binson?], both of Philadelphia city. We wish them a long and happy life.

articles.headline: Fine Cake Bakery, Confectionary and Ice Cream Saloon (advertisement)
articles.summary: Fine Cake Bakery, Confectionary and Ice Cream Saloon, No. 80[1/2] South Street. Ellis J. Peer would announce that he keeps constantly on hand a general assortment of all kinds of Cakes, Creams, Jellies, and Pastries. Festivals, Balls, and Private Parties served upon the shortest notice. Jan. 19--1m. [Recurring; captured once.]

articles.headline: Teachers of the piano (advertisements)
articles.summary: Miss L. H. Robertson, Teacher of the Piano, No. 1150 S. Eleventh Street, Philadelphia. -- Miss M. E. Marsall [sic], Teacher of the Piano Forte, Residence No. 419 South Thirteenth Street, Philadelphia. [Race of advertisers not stated; this ad block is shared with the white-run Christian Instructor -- see notes.]

articles.headline: The Death of the Rev. John Cornish (poem)
articles.author: C. Danfield [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Elegiac poem: '...Voices from heaven are in the still air... As Cornish' spirit wings empyrean space...' Signed C. Danfield [VERIFY].

articles.headline: The Daughters of Conference
articles.summary: The Daughters of Conference, Bethel Church, Philadelphia, met in Bethel Church on last Thursday night, the 17th inst., to have a lecture delivered to them, to increase their fund. The Rev. J. M. Brown, being in the city, delivered a discourse to them from the 2d Chapter of Habakkuk, 4th verse...

articles.headline: Congratulations
articles.summary: We are continually receiving letters from our friends, congratulating us on behalf of our paper; among which is one from our friend and scholar of Hamilton, O., Mr. A. J. Anderson, who is one of the leading Trustees of the Wilberforce University... We also have one from our friend, Mr. Wiggins, which appears in this week's paper.

articles.headline: Protracted Meeting (Little Wesley)
articles.summary: The Rev. C. Woodyard is holding a protracted meeting in his charge, Little Wesley. May the Lord guide the battle.

articles.headline: Dedication (Gouldtown)
articles.summary: The Rev. Bishop Nazrey will, the Lord willing, dedicate a new Church, built by Rev. Jos. Smith, at Gouldtown, N. J., next Sabbath, the 27th inst., at half-past 10 o'clock, A. M.
people: pastor, builder of the Gouldtown church (Rev.)

articles.headline: Quarterly Meeting (Bethel)
articles.summary: Rev. J. Woodlin's quarterly meeting, in Bethel Church, on Sabbath, the 27th inst.

articles.headline: Notice (Publication Society meeting)
articles.summary: The Publication Society will meet next Thursday evening in Bethel Church. All the members and friends are requested to meet, as the cause is a worthy one. We bespeak a full house for them. Mark, it is the first Thursday in February.

articles.headline: Death of Brother Carr
articles.author: Sarah A. Carr
articles.summary: We publish the following letter that we have received from Miss Carr... Another good man, a local preacher, Snider Carr, has fallen from the ranks of laborers... Gaysport, Jan. 18th, 1861. Mr. E. Weaver.--Dear Brother:--I drop you these few lines to inform you that my dear father departed this life on last Sabbath morning... [Non-Philadelphia: Gaysport, Pa.; names in summary only.]

articles.headline: Letter from Friend Wiggins
articles.author: Nathaniel Wiggins
articles.summary: Rev. Elisha Weaver:--Dear Sir:--It is with pleasure that I have just read the second number of your valuable paper, The Christian Recorder. Allow me to say that it is a perfect triumph... I shall contribute to its columns occasionally.

articles.headline: California Mission
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: I will here call the attention of the ministers and members of the different districts in the A. M. E. Connexion, to the doings of the General Conference of 1860, at Pittsburgh, in relation to the California Mission... The Ohio Conference had taken action to raise their proportional part, and send it as follows: to the Rev. Stephen Smith, No. 319 Lombard Street, Philadelphia. Send it by Adams & Co.'s Express...
people: receiver of California Mission funds (Rev.), No. 319 Lombard Street

articles.headline: Confectionery (editorial puff for Mr. Peer)
articles.summary: It will be seen by referring to an advertisement or card, that our friend, Mr. Peer, in South street, is prepared to accommodate his friends at a very short notice. We hope he may get a fair share of patronage, for he and his good lady keep excellent articles.
people: confectioner, South street (Mr.) = Ellis J. Peer
wife of Mr. Peer ('his good lady')

articles.headline: Undertaker (editorial puff for Mrs. Duterte)
articles.summary: Mrs. Duterte's advertisement will be found under that head, in one of our columns. We would recommend her as being always ready to accommodate any one in her line of business. We hope she may receive a fair share of patronage, for she is worthy of it.

articles.headline: Notice (Box 430; General Conference Minutes; Free-will Offering)
articles.summary: Our Correspondents and Subscribers will please take notice that all letters... must be directed to Box No. 430, Philadelphia, Pa. We would be very glad if those brethren who received the General Conference Minutes would have the kindness to forward us the money for them... also those brethren who hold the money called the Free-will Offering, should obey the General Conference.

articles.headline: Colored Men Cannot Write (editorial)
articles.summary: [A white acquaintance] considers himself a scholar... He said he did not know of more than one or two colored persons who could write... The experience of not a few of our race has been much like our own: left a fatherless and motherless boy at the age of ten years, in old North Carolina... [Autobiographical passage by editor Weaver.]

articles.headline: Banneker Institute (resolutions on the death of Jesse Ewing Glasgow, Jr.)
articles.author: John W. Simpson
articles.summary: At a special meeting held Jan. 16, 1861, the decease of Mr. Jesse Ewing Glasgow, Jr., was announced, whereupon a committee, consisting of Messrs. O. V. Catto, W. H. Minton and H. B. Black, was appointed to draft resolutions... Resolved, That copies of these resolutions be sent to the family of the deceased and the University of Edinburgh... John W. Simpson, President. (Attest,) J. C. White, Secretary.
people: deceased member; student, University of Edinburgh
secretary, Banneker Institute (printed 'J. C. White'; identified as Jacob C. White Jr., Banneker secretary -- Michiko 2026-10-31)

articles.headline: Observations of Bishop Nazrey: The People and their Occupation
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Commencing in the western part of Pennsylvania, we find a large portion of the colored people, of both sexes, depending entirely for a living upon the steamboats plying on the various rivers and lakes... [Western/Ohio/Michigan settlements; non-Philadelphia.]

articles.headline: Devotional Choir Singing (no. 1)
articles.author: A. Burris
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--You will please pardon the boldness I have assumed in imposing the following article upon your columns... we know of several competent vocalists among our people, such as a E. T. G., or T. C. B., or a H. S., a Mr. A. W. L. Those, with a few others, are all Philadelphia can boast of as vocalists...

articles.headline: Curious Facts in Science
articles.author: B.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Resuming the subject where we left off in our last, we purpose saying somewhat more of the curious property of Allotropism in Carbon... [Signed 'B.']

articles.headline: The Arts and Sciences (porcelain and pottery)
articles.author: Baisnea [VERIFY]
articles.summary: We shall not enter into a history of this branch of the industrial arts... we hope that that gun, fired by Mr. H. Garnett, of New York, at our 'Negro Aristocracy,' may effectually clear the atmosphere... We think a company of young men might be formed for the purpose of manufacturing children's toys...

articles.headline: The Rights of Colored People (Goines vs. McCandless)
articles.author: W. S.
articles.summary: Decision of the District Court against Colored People Riding in the City Railway Cars. Mr. Editor:--The colored people of Philadelphia, as you know, have, within the last week, had a second edition of the Dred Scott decision, from the District Court of Pennsylvania, sitting here, in the case of George W. Goines vs. McCandless. The defendant, McCandless, was a conductor on one of the city railways, who, some time back, ejected Mr. G. in a forcible manner from the cars on account of his color... Philadelphia, Jan. 23d, 1861.
people: plaintiff, ejected from city railway car

articles.headline: A Scene in Philadelphia: The Ups and Downs of Life
articles.summary: [In a] neat, quiet, back street there is now living a young man and his wife, with their three children... The father, who learned the trade of [...] plating, found himself... entirely out of employment... [Unnamed family; summary from OCR, no names.]

articles.headline: Mrs. H. S. Duterte, General Undertaker and Furnisher (advertisement)
articles.summary: Mrs. H. S. Duterte, General Undertaker and Furnisher, respectfully informs her friends and the public, that she still continues the Undertaking business at the old establishment, No. 634 Lombard St., and being thankful for past favors, hopes still to obtain a share of the patronage of the public. Ready made Coffins always on hand. Also a handsome Hearse and Carriages, with careful drivers... [Recurring; captured once.]
people: proprietor, general undertaker (Mrs.), No. 634 [VERIFY] Lombard St.

articles.headline: A New Class of Emigrants (news item)
articles.summary: Within a few weeks, some seventy-five colored families, who have emigrated from Charleston, S. C., have come to this city, and taken up their abode in the negro quarter of the town. They left their old homes because of the going into effect, in South Carolina, of a law which requires all free negroes to wear a badge... Their arrival here has caused quite a sensation in colored circles. I understand that New York has also received a share of these emigrants.--Cor. of World.

articles.headline: Our Disciplines / Notice to correspondents / Bristol payments
articles.summary: Will the brethren send in their orders, get the Disciplines, sell them, and forward us the money... Our Bristol friends are paying up their subscriptions. We acknowledge the following: From Theodore Freeman, $2.00; Miss Matilda Tenyick, $2.00; Peter Tenyick, $2.00. From Miss Leana Page, Burlington, $1.00. Our city subscribers--those who have paid their dollar and a half, will only have to pay the carriers one cent, and those who have paid nothing must pay the carrier four cents on delivery.

articles.headline: Revivals
articles.summary: A number of churches are holding a series of meetings. Among which is Little Wesley A. M. E. C., Pastor, Rev. C. Woodyard. Also, the Rev. Mr. Cooper, pastor of St. John's M. E. Church, is having a glorious time. We preached for them on last Friday night, the 25th inst... [Also notes Rev. H. J. Young, New Bedford, Mass.]
people: pastor, St. John's M. E. Church (Rev.)

articles.headline: News from Churches
articles.summary: We received a letter from our good brother Strother, of Richmond, Ind., stating that he is engaged in carrying on a protracted meeting... Also, one from Rev. W. H. Waters, of Baltimore... Also, a letter from our young and esteemed brother, Henry M. Turner... Rev. Daniel Moore, of Washington... brother Rue, of Newport, R. I.... Rev. A. C. Crippen, of Newark, N. J., accompanied with some seven subscribers... Rev. Jesse Divine, of Columbus, Ohio. [All non-Philadelphia; names in summary only.]

articles.headline: Letter from Friend Wiggins
articles.author: Nathaniel Wiggins
articles.summary: January 2[?], 1861. To Rev. Elisha Weaver, Editor of Christian Recorder: Rev. and Dear Sir:--I have now before me the 2d No. of your valuable paper... My temporal business requires me to be in the presence of our most influential citizens, to whom I have shown the Christian Recorder... one, a distinguished member of the bar, said that the people of color were just beginning to display the lights from under the bushel.

articles.headline: Episcopal Visits
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: I will visit Bordentown, N. J., March 1st, and will remain in that circuit until the [4th]. I shall then leave for Princeton, on which circuit I shall remain from the 8th to the 11th. Leave thence for [New Bruns]wick... Next visit Burlington, and remain on that circuit until the 21st. I will be on Westchester circuit on the 23d... until the 29th, and will leave then for Penningtonville circuit and remain in that circuit until the [5th?] of April. Next visit Columbia circuit, and remain about a week.

articles.headline: Our Visit to Gouldtown
articles.summary: Saturday morning, the 26th inst., at 9 o'clock A. M., Rev. Bishop Nazrey and I stepped aboard of the boat which soon conveyed us across the Delaware River to Camden, where we were very politely asked by the conductor of the West Jersey Railroad Company to take back seats in the car... Among the first whom our eyes beheld was the Rev. Joseph Smith, pastor of the church which we went down to dedicate...
people: young man who conveyed bishop and editor; near Gouldtown

articles.headline: Observations of Bishop Nazrey: The Religious Condition of our People in [the West]
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: They have, as a general thing, good buildings as places of worship, which are generally paid for. The attendance is reasonably good... [Western circuits; non-Philadelphia.]

articles.headline: Our Duty (to the Commonwealth)
articles.summary: What are the obligations and duties of the colored population of Pennsylvania in the present crisis? It has been our good fortune to become the residents of a State whose ancestral virtue and humanity bear the indelible record that she was the first... to secure, by legislative enactments, the liberty of her bondmen!... (To be continued.)

articles.headline: Devotional Choir Singing (no. 2)
articles.author: A. B. [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I hope you will pardon me for again intruding myself upon your columns. In our last article we stated that a greater portion of choristers had lost... the spirit of devotional psalmody... [Signature faint; continuation of A. Burris, 26 Jan.]

articles.headline: The Bishop's Allowance
articles.author: Joshua Woodlin
articles.summary: Brother Weaver:--Permit me to inform the ministers who have charges of circuits and stations in the Philadelphia and New England Districts... that our beloved Bishop, Willis Nazrey, has arrived here some time since with his family, to preside over the said Districts... The Conference having appointed me District Book Steward... The Bishop's address is Philadelphia, Pa., 606 Pine Street, above Sixth. Yours fraternally, Joshua Woodlin, District Book Steward.
people: bishop; residence 606 Pine Street above Sixth

articles.headline: The Arts and Sciences (proposals: industrial societies, 'Industrial Congress')
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--The proposal which we have to make is this--that our young men and women form themselves into societies of six or more members, for the following... purposes... 5th. To elect annually or otherwise a delegate for the organization of an 'Industrial Congress'... [Signature not legible on film.]

articles.headline: Reply to 'W. S.' on the Goines railway-car case
articles.author: [illegible]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I notice an article in your paper of the 26th instant, by 'W. S.,' who has attempted to review the recent decision in the District Court, in the case of Goines vs. McCandless... Our counsel were W. S. Peirce [VERIFY], Esq., and Ex-Judge of the Supreme Court, Mr. Knox... I am informed the case is to be taken to the Supreme Court... let him attend the meetings that will be called for the purpose of raising funds... Phila., Jan. 28th, 1861.

articles.headline: Meetings (quarterly meeting notices)
articles.summary: Rev. L. C. Speaks' Quarterly Meeting is (this) Saturday and Sabbath evenings, the 9th and 10th insts. Rev. John Cornish's Quarterly Meeting is at Old Chester on the 17th inst., and at New Chester on the 24th.
people: pastor; quarterly meetings at Old Chester and New Chester (Rev.)

articles.headline: Anniversary (Ladies of the John Cornish Society)
articles.summary: The ladies of the John Cornish Society held their Anniversary on Wednesday evening, the 10th inst. Mrs. Carter, their President, seems to be well qualified for that position; she is assisted by Mrs. Harris. The Annual Report, read by Mrs. Seymour, was a very interesting document.
people: assistant to the president, John Cornish Society
read the Annual Report, John Cornish Society

articles.headline: Donation Visit (A.M.E. Church, Trenton, N.J.)
articles.summary: We learn that the members of the A. M. E. Church, Trenton, N. J., paid their Pastor, Rev. J. P. Campbell, a donation visit, on Tuesday, the 5th inst. Some $17 cash and about $20 in presents was the result.

articles.headline: Visit to New York
articles.summary: We left the 'City of Brotherly Love' on Saturday, the 2d inst., at 11 o'clock, a.m., for New York City, and arrived there at 4 o'clock, p.m. We stopped in at Mrs. Jones', near Bethel Church, and had a short conversation with this good sister. (Editor Weaver's trip: Rev. [George] Weir, Bethel Church NY; Rev. L. C. Speaks, Bridge Street Church, Brooklyn; Rev. Wm. Moore, Flushing; Watson of the New York Circuit; Mr. and Mrs. Champion, Brooklyn. Notes the paper supplies over 410 copies per week in Philadelphia. All named persons are New York; not linked.)

articles.headline: News from the Churches
articles.author: J. P. Campbell
articles.summary: Dear Brother Weaver: The reappearance of the Christian Recorder is hailed by many as a most glorious advent. I have near me a letter from a most distinguished minister, an elder of the New England Conference ... (Names as supporters: Wm. Moore, J. A. Shorter, H. L. Brooks, J. Turner of St. Louis, J. M. Brown, A. W. Wayman, W. H. Waters, S. L. Hammond, W. D. W. Schureman, J. Woodlin, 'with our bishops'. Reports H. J. Young of New Bedford; Rev. Theodore Gould of the Princeton circuit raising funds for a new brick church at Princeton; Trenton circuit paid off church at Pennington; Princeton circuit +39 members, Trenton circuit +44. Brother Waters of Baltimore $3.42 and Mr. Edward M. Thomas of Washington acknowledged. Dated Trenton, Jan. [day illegible], 1861.)
people: named as supporter of the Recorder (Rev.)
named as supporter of the Recorder

articles.headline: Our Duty, No. 2
articles.summary: In a former article we aimed to direct attention to the past policy of Pennsylvania, with respect to our rights and privileges ... and to point out the corresponding obligations imposed on us, as colored citizens, for the rich blessing of freedom and happiness we enjoy. (Invokes 'the proud historic deeds of Richard Allen, Absalom Jones, James Foster [sic, prob. Forten], Jeffrey, Johnson, Davis, Black, Durham, and Vashon'. To be continued.)

articles.headline: Thoughts on Marriage
articles.author: W. D. W. Schureman
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: I purpose writing a few practical thoughts on the above-mentioned subject. Marriage is the union of sexes, under matrimonial obligations. It is the proper mode to carry out a Divine mandate.

articles.headline: The Arts and Sciences: Smelting and Refining
articles.author: Brister
articles.summary: Our attention has been frequently called to this subject, from the fact, that the sweepings from the benches and floors of the workshops of the workers in gold and silver ... are put through a process by which the precious metal is extracted. (Closes with 'a word on improvement in business': criticizes 'some of our men on Second Street in the clothes business' still in 'the same dark and dismal cellars' as twelve years ago. To be continued.)

articles.headline: Devotional Choir Singing
articles.author: A. B.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: In our last article we mentioned a few faults with regard to devotional choir singing. We proceed to speak of a few more ... (States there are 'some sixteen or eighteen churches in this city, and among them all, there are not more than three properly trained choirs'.)

articles.headline: New clothing store (editorial puff)
articles.summary: [Opening lines illegible] ... at his new clothing store both new and second hand clothes, for the accommodation of all his customers. It is one of the cheapest, if not the cheapest store in the city. We hope all will give him a call. He has not only subscribed for the paper ... for one year. (Proprietor's name illegible on film; possibly F. Champion of Brooklyn, whose ad is on p3 and whom the editor visited, but not legible.)

articles.headline: Festival (Camden, N.J.)
articles.summary: A Festival will be given for the benefit of the ... [Sabbath School?] ... of the A. M. E. Church, Camden, N. J., commencing ... [dates illegible].

articles.headline: Official Notice (Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity)
articles.summary: A grand demonstration of the entire Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity, will be held at Bethel Church, on Thursday evening February 7th, 1861. All the officers and members of the grand and subordinate tabernacles, in and out of the State, are requested to meet in the basement ...
people: Grand Worthy Superior, Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity (Rev.)

articles.headline: Lecture (Union Baptist Church)
articles.summary: The Rev. J. W[heaton?] Smith will deliver one of his interesting lectures at the Union Baptist church, Little Pine Street, above Sixth, on Tuesday, the 12th, at 8 o'clock, P. M. Subject: 'The Discoveries made by him, in the Holy Land.'

[Prints extracts from the Baltimore Exchange and Baltimore Sun: the Board of Police Commissioners will enforce the Maryland law against non-resident free negroes, so AME Baltimore Conference members from Virginia, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Delaware may not attend in April. Signer not found in the column.]

articles.headline: Letter on Bishop Payne's Anglo-African article (defence of the General and Executive Committees)
articles.author: [illegible] Moore [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Rev. and Dear Brother Weaver: Editor of the Christian Recorder:--Dear Sir, in looking over the Anglo-African for March 9th, I saw an article signed D. A. Payne, which article calls upon the ministers of the A. M. E. Church. Now, sir, I am one of that class. [Signature faded: '... Moore' with an illegible place line; VERIFY.]

articles.headline: Letter from Rev. H. J. Young (Detroit)
articles.author: H. J. Young
articles.summary: Rev. and Dear Bro. Weaver:--This will inform you that I left New Bedford on the 22d of February, to visit my family in Chatham, C.W. ... [Detroit revival under Rev. J. Warren; reprint from the New Bedford Standard. Non-Philadelphia; not linked.]

articles.headline: Letter replying to Bishop John H. Hopkins of Vermont on human equality
articles.author: Johnson Woodlin [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--Having received the first number of the Recorder, I was much pleased with its appearance. ... Among the many passing events of the day, there appeared in the Sunday Dispatch, of your city, a letter, signed 'John H. Hopkins, Bishop of the Diocese of Vermont,' in which article there are more deadly blows aimed at the Declaration of American Independence.

articles.headline: The Divinity of Christ
articles.author: C. Woodyard
articles.summary: Dear Editor--I take my pen in hand to write on the greatest of all subjects, namely, the character of Christ. (To be continued.)

articles.headline: Advice to Our Young People, No. IV
articles.author: W. S. [VERIFY]
articles.summary: 'Honesty is the best policy.' Our young people cannot ground themselves too firmly on this foundation. (To be continued.)

articles.headline: Notice: concert for the Social, Civil and Statistical Association
articles.summary: NOTICE. [Faded on the film.] ... on Monday evening next, 25th inst., ... Hall, for the benefit of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of the Colored People of Pennsylvania ... [Most of the text is illegible; the Mar 30 report (CR_1861-03-30 p2) confirms it was the Hutchinson Family concert at Sansom Street Hall.]

articles.headline: Dr. Brown's Lecture
articles.summary: Dr. H. J. Brown of Burlington, New Jersey, paid us a visit a few days ago, and gave two very interesting and highly important lectures upon phrenology, physiology and the laws of health.
people: lecturer on phrenology and physiology, of Burlington, N.J. (Dr.)

articles.headline: The Funeral of James Prosser (Domestic News)
articles.summary: The Funeral of James Prosser.--Among the [first line illegible] ... the late James Prosser will long be remembered. Prosser was to Philadelphia what Downing is to New York, except that Prosser leaves about $2?,000 [VERIFY figure] as the result of his thrift and integrity, while Downing is worth at least five times that amount. For nearly half a century Mr. Prosser kept a restaurant in Market street, and was favorably known to the greater portion of the business community.
people: deceased; restaurant keeper in Market street for nearly half a century

articles.headline: Obituary: Mrs. Mary Ingraw [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Died in this city, Feb. 12th [VERIFY], Mrs. Mary Ingraw [VERIFY; probably INGRAM], after a lingering illness, which she bore with Christian fortitude. Her age was [illegible] years. Our loss is her infinite gain.

articles.headline: Poem on the death of Miss Caroline Parks (Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School)
articles.summary: The following beautiful lines were written by a youthful member of the Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School, of Philadelphia, which, on account of the youth of the author, and the subject of the lines (Miss Caroline Parks) having been a member of the School, it was unanimously agreed by the school that they be published in the Anglo-African, Recorder, and Royalist [VERIFY]. Miss Parks, it will be remembered, was brutally murdered a few months ago by a young man in California.
people: deceased; former member of Shiloh Baptist Sabbath School, Philadelphia; murdered in California (Miss)

articles.headline: To Our City Patrons
articles.summary: We wish our city subscribers would be particular, and try to pay the carriers, for we are depending upon the income of our paper every week. We would much rather that you would pay your four cents on delivery of the paper. Remember that the carriers cannot deliver the papers for nothing; and if any one of our subscribers do not get their papers, please let us know, and we will see whose route it is in, and have it attended to.

articles.headline: Singing of the Hutchinson Family
articles.summary: The Social, Civil and Statistical Association of Colored People, of Pennsylvania, a Society of a high literary character of this city, obtained the services of the Hutchinson family, whose fame is abroad, to give them a Concert in Sansom Street Hall, on Monday night, the 25th inst.
people: 'our noted and distinguished friend and Professor', performed with the Hutchinsons

articles.headline: News from the Churches
articles.summary: Rev. G. H. Graham, of Cincinnati, O., writes that God has very graciously poured out his Spirit upon the Church. [Also Rev. B. L. Brooks of Louisville, Ky.; Joseph P. Shreeves [VERIFY] of Bridgeport, Conn.; Rev. William H. Turner of Wilmington, Del.; Nelson H. Turpin of Detroit, licensed to exhort. None Philadelphia; not linked.]

articles.headline: Our Paper
articles.summary: It is now three months since the appearance of the first number of the Christian Recorder. It was prophesied by some persons that the Recorder would not survive three weeks.

articles.headline: Philadelphia Tribune
articles.summary: We have before us the Philadelphia Tribune, published by a Stock Company, weekly, at the S. W. corner of Second and Brown Streets. It is a good size, fair type, and well conducted. We like this paper for many reasons, one of which is, because it has the right view of national subjects.

articles.headline: The Christian Chronicle
articles.summary: We also have on our table this weekly, Christian paper, edited by Rev. James S. Dickerson. It is nearly the size of the Christian Recorder. [White Baptist paper; editor not linked.]

articles.headline: Letter from Bishop Nazrey (visit to the New Jersey circuits)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--As I have always felt it to be a duty that I owed to the church to speak to and of the church through its organ ... I propose to give them a few words on the different subjects that have come under my observation while visiting some of our Circuits in New Jersey. My first visit was paid to Bordentown Circuit.
people: AME member at Allentown, N.J.; rents a 150-acre farm at $800 a year, host of the Bishop (Brother)

articles.headline: The Winter Lectures at the Institute for Colored Youth
articles.summary: On Thursday evening, 21st inst., Mrs. S. M. Douglass delivered a scientific lecture on the circulation of blood in creative beings, the circulation of fluid in plants, in birds and reptiles, &c., to a crowded house of ladies and gentlemen.
people: lecturer at the Institute for Colored Youth (Mrs.)
Principal of the Institute for Colored Youth; gave the first lecture of the season (Prof.)

articles.headline: Baltimore Methodist Conference: attempted separation from the Northern Church
articles.summary: The Baltimore Methodist Conference, which has been in session at Staunton, Va., adjourned on Saturday, after adopting a plan for separation from the Northern Church. [M. E. Church, white; general news.]

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: We have received a very interesting letter from Rev. L. S. Lewis, of Boston, Mass., containing five dollars. [Also John H. Beal; Mr. William Nesbit of Altoona, Pa., and Rev. Alexander Johnson on the same circuit, $5; Rev. W. H. Waters of Baltimore, $2. None Philadelphia; not linked.]

articles.headline: Bro. Logan's Quarterly Meeting
articles.author: Spencer Logan
articles.summary: Philadelphia, March 2? [VERIFY day], 1861. My Quarterly Meeting will take place in New Hope on April 21st, at Buckingham Mountains on April 28th, at Newtown on May 5th, and at Attleborough on May 12th.

articles.headline: Letters Received
articles.summary: We have received a letter from Rev. A. McIntosh, of Springfield, Ill., one of the General Committee. ... this was the business of the Executive Committee, composed of Rev. Messrs. Moore, Schureman, and Waters. [Also reports from Rev. Daniel Cooper of Gallipolis, Ohio, the death of Mr. Elijah Anderson of Cleveland, Ohio, lately imprisoned in the Kentucky Penitentiary, who died in Kentucky.]
people: member of the Executive Committee (Rev.) [printed 'Schureman' surname only here]

articles.headline: Revival at Salem Church, Salem, N. J.
articles.author: Peter Gardner
articles.summary: Mr. Editor:--I wish to let you know that God, in mercy, has favored our Zion, at Salem, N. J., at the last Quarterly Meeting. ... The meeting was protracted two weeks longer. ... Ten persons turned their backs upon the powers of darkness ... A few backsliders were reclaimed, and the church revived.

articles.headline: Sanctification
articles.author: Peter Gardner
articles.summary: Write it upon pages of adamant, that the corroding tooth of time may never obliterate its legibility. ... Reader, is this your experience?

articles.headline: Chapters on Ethnology, Chapter Sixth: The Wars of Antiquity
articles.summary: When sufficient time had elapsed, after the dispersion of mankind, for the development of great nationalities, a spirit of daring and a love of martial glory began to manifest itself.

articles.headline: The Executive Department of the General Book Committee, in Reply to Rev. D. A. Payne
articles.author: W. Moore, W. H. Waters, W. D. W. Schureman (Executive Committee)
articles.summary: Phila., March 11th, 1861. Mr. Editor:--In looking over the columns of the Anglo-African of the 9th inst., we find an article entitled 'The Christian Recorder, or Evil Behind a Right,' over the signature of our worthy and efficient New School Bishop, Rev. Daniel A. Payne.
people: Executive Committee, co-signer (Rev.; of Flushing, N.Y., per CR_1861-03-23)
General Book Steward and Editor defended (Rev.)

articles.headline: Letter from Henry Davis (Bishop Nazrey's visit to the Burlington circuit)
articles.author: Henry Davis
articles.summary: Brother Weaver:--According to appointment, Bishop Nazrey and his wife made their appearance on the 15th of March, about noon. He preached in Burlington in the evening, from the first Psalm, third verse; and on the 16th, in Clarksborough. A corner stone for a new church was laid by the Bishop, and the minister having the charge of the Burlington circuit.

articles.headline: Notice (Bishop Nazrey on Bishop Payne's Anglo-African article)
articles.author: W. Nazrey
articles.summary: To the Readers and Friends of the Christian Recorder, or organ of the A. M. E. Church:--As there has lately appeared in the Anglo-African an article purporting to come from the Rev. D. A. Payne, one of the Bishops of the A. M. E. church, asking the ministers of said church certain questions in relation to the existence of the Christian Recorder, reason and propriety prompt me to doubt Bishop Payne being its author.

articles.headline: Reply of Brother Wiggins (Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity)
articles.author: Nathaniel Wiggins
articles.summary: To the Editor of the Christian Recorder, Rev. Elisha Weaver--Dear Sir:--Our attention has been called to a notice in your valuable paper of March 16th, 1861, of an article signed by G. W. S., G. W. N. S., P. G. W. U. S., G. G. D. M., &c., endeavoring to throw a stigma upon the Independent order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity, on account of an article signed H. G. B., in a previous number of your paper, in reference to the death of our sister and fellow member, Anna B. Bedford.
people: deceased member of the Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity

articles.headline: Episcopal Visits
articles.author: Willis Nazrey
articles.summary: I propose visiting Frankford circuit, April 13th; Salem circuit, April 20th; Greenwich circuit, April 27th; Reading circuit, May 4th. It is possible these appointments may be changed somewhat in order to meet other demands.

events.name: Publication Society of Philadelphia -- meeting called to organize young people's society in aid of the paper
events.location: No. 619 Pine street, Philadelphia (Weaver's house / AME Book Depository)
events.description: Editor Elisha Weaver notes the Publication Society 'was organized some years ago to assist in publishing a paper'; 'Mrs. Laws, I believe, is the President.' He calls the young ladies and gentlemen in favor of the undertaking to meet at 'our house, No. 619 Pine street, on Monday evening, the 21st' [evening hour printed, about 7 1/2 o'clock] to organize themselves into a society to aid in establishing the Recorder. Follow-up: CR_1861-01-26 p2 announces the Publication Society will meet in Bethel Church the first Thursday in February.

events.name: Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's quarterly meeting
events.description: Announced in the Quarterly Meetings notice for the coming Sabbath.

events.name: Rev. Peter Gardiner's quarterly meeting, Woodbury N.J.
events.description: Quarterly meeting to be held Saturday and Sabbath, the 19th and 20th January 1861 (date given = first day).

events.name: Rev. Robertson's quarterly meeting at Bristol; Recorder subscribers enrolled
events.description: Weaver spent 'last Sunday' (13 Jan 1861) at Bristol at the quarterly meeting of 'our Rev. and esteemed father, Robertson' [owner's ruling: = Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford]. Robertson presented the book concern and paper; 50 copies sold, about 20 subscribers. Weaver remarks the young ladies showed more interest in improvement of mind than the young men and wishes the 'handsome little church' had backs to its seats. Bristol subscribers as printed (each $2.00 unless noted): Miss Ann Louisa Williams ($1.00); Mrs. Sarah Smith; Mrs. Mary Dean; Mr. Josiah Ross [VERIFY surname], Bridgewater P.O.; Mr. Peter Teneyick; [Eli]zabeth Derry [first name partly lost]; Mrs. Harriet Freeman; Mrs. Mary Johnson; Mrs. Elizabeth Sharp (paid $1); [Miss?] Anna E. Fry (paid) [VERIFY]; [Car]oline Williams [first name partly lost]; [Mr.] Henry Williams [VERIFY]; Henry Blake; Theodore Freeman; Charles Anderson, Bridgewater; Mr. James Tilminion [VERIFY]; Sylvester Buckus; Mrs. Adeline Banks; Miss Matilda Teneyick. Burlington subscribers 'not inserted in our first issue' (page torn at left, several names truncated): Mrs. Mary S. Thompson (paid) $1; Mrs. Ann Harris $1; Mrs. Lydia Ann Thomas $1; Miss Lucy Ann Cumming $2; [Mr.] Aaron Johnson (paid) $2; [...]ckson $1; [...] Stidum (paid) $1; [...]y (paid) $1; [...]ry Sels[?] $1; Sarah Page $1; [Cha]rles Williams $1; [...]dman Dutt[on?], Columbus, New Jersey $2; [...] Still, Allentown, N. J. $2.

events.name: Protracted meeting at the AME mission church (Zion City Mission), Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. Stephen Smith, pastor of the mission, has held a protracted meeting there 'which seems to have resulted in good'; the editor has attended on several occasions. (The mission is listed as 'Zion City Mission, Phila.' in the Bishop's Allowance table, CR_1861-02-02 p2.)

events.name: Weaver's Wednesday-night meeting at Frankford with father Robertson
events.description: Weather unfavorable but friends turned out; Weaver preached a short sermon and presented the paper, disposing of all copies he had (about sixty). Rev. H. Davis, a local preacher, and his son undertake to take one hundred copies per week to supply Frankford.

events.name: A. M. E. Preachers' Association (Philadelphia district) -- weekly meetings
events.description: Per W. D. W. Schureman: organized 'last August' (1860) on Weaver's proposal, after an earlier attempt at weekly meetings by J. P. Campbell (then general book steward) and others; meets in Bethel Church on Tuesday mornings at 9 o'clock A.M. Object: to correct errors historical, Biblical, logical or grammatical. Order: chairman appointed, scribe elected, singing and prayer, roll called alphabetically, each minister states the past week's ministerial labour, text and manner of treatment, open to criticism; a theological or Discipline question discussed each meeting.

events.name: Marriage of William Stokes [VERIFY] and Anna Robinson [VERIFY]
events.description: Notice under 'Married': the editor ('we') joined in marriage 'our friends Mr. William Sto[k]es and Miss Anna Ro[...]n, both of Philadelphia city.' Both surnames are faint/blurred at the right column edge; readings uncertain.

events.name: Daughters of Conference (Bethel Church) -- benefit lecture by Rev. J. M. Brown
events.description: The Daughters of Conference of Bethel Church met Thursday night 17 Jan to hear a lecture to increase their fund; Rev. J. M. Brown, in the city, preached from Habakkuk 2:4; a collection was taken for the society. Officers: President Mrs. Williams; Treasurer Mrs. Highgate. The editor credits the sisters with 'the good they have done for some forty years' (i.e., organized c. 1820).

events.name: Protracted meeting at Little Wesley AME Church
events.description: Rev. C. Woodyard, pastor, holding a protracted meeting in his charge (reported 26 Jan; still continuing per 2 Feb 'Revivals').

events.name: Rev. J. Woodlin's quarterly meeting at Bethel
events.description: Announced quarterly meeting of Rev. J. Woodlin (Joshua Woodlin, who signs as District Book Steward on 2 Feb) at Bethel Church.

events.name: Publication Society meeting at Bethel Church
events.description: Members and friends requested to attend; 'Mark, it is the first Thursday in February.' (Date computed: first Thursday of Feb 1861 = 7 Feb.) Follows the organizing call of 21 Jan (CR_1861-01-19 p2).

events.name: Banneker Institute special meeting -- resolutions on death of Jesse Ewing Glasgow, Jr.
events.description: Special meeting announced the death of member Jesse Ewing Glasgow, Jr. (student at the University of Edinburgh, near completion of his curriculum). Committee to draft resolutions: Messrs. O. V. Catto, W. H. Minton and H. B. Black. Resolutions call his death an irreparable loss to the community and Institute, 'one potent and living evidence of the black man's ability in the higher walks of knowledge', tender sympathy to his family and condolence to the University of Edinburgh, and order copies sent to the family and the University. Signed John W. Simpson, President; attest J. C. White, Secretary.
attendees: secretary (printed 'J. C. White'; identified as Jacob C. White Jr., Banneker secretary -- Michiko 2026-10-31)

events.name: Revival at St. John's M. E. Church; Weaver preaches
events.location: St. John's M. E. Church [Philadelphia, as implied]
events.description: Rev. Mr. Cooper, pastor of St. John's M. E. Church, 'is having a glorious time'; Weaver preached there Friday night 25 Jan; afterward Cooper 'without any exhortation at all, said, Come; and before the word was clearly from his lips, the altar was crowded.' Same notice: Little Wesley A.M.E. Church (Rev. C. Woodyard) holding a series of meetings. City of St. John's not stated explicitly.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's spring episcopal visitation, NJ and Pa. circuits of the Philadelphia Conference
events.location: Bordentown, Princeton, New Brunswick, Burlington, West Chester, Penningtonville and Columbia circuits
events.description: Itinerary as printed (signature faint, read as W. Nazrey): Bordentown N.J. from March 1 'until the [4th?]'; Princeton circuit 8th-11th; [New Bruns]wick 11th to [1?]th; Burlington circuit until the 21st; Westchester circuit on the 23d, remaining until the 29th (the elder to inform him where to meet); then Penningtonville circuit until the [5th?] of April; then Columbia circuit about a week. Ministers asked to arrange preaching points.

events.name: Dedication of Trinity Church (African M. E.), Gouldtown, N.J.
events.location: Gouldtown Church, near Bridgeton, N. J.
events.description: Weaver's narrative. Sat 26 Jan: Weaver and Bishop Nazrey crossed to Camden; West Jersey Railroad conductor asked them to take back seats; by rail to Woodbury and stage (driver 'whose name, we think, is Mr. Snider' [VERIFY]) about thirty miles to Bridgeton, arriving about 4 P.M., met by Rev. Joseph Smith, pastor. Dined at the house of a brother 'whom they called Bishop' [surname or nickname unclear]; young William Stewart drove them to his father's house near Gouldtown, about two miles from Bridgeton; 'Sister Stewart, his good lady' served tea. Sun 27 Jan (snow 4-5 inches): at 11 o'clock the bishop, pastor and Weaver marched in, other ministers following; the trustees delivered the key; Smith and Weaver assisted the bishop in the consecration; the church was named 'Trinity Church, of the African M. E. Church'; bishop preached Zech. 2:5; $27 collected. 3 P.M. Weaver preached 1 Chron. 28:9, $23.50 collected (total fifty dollars and some cents); at night the bishop preached Gal. v. 9. Church about 45 by 37 feet, two carpeted aisles, pulpit decorated by 'the Gouldtown ladies', front gallery seating over one hundred; credit to the trustees. Mon 28 Jan: brother Stewart drove them to Bridgeton; returned via Woodbury, where the car conductor again required back seats.

events.name: Assessment of the Bishop's allowance on Philadelphia District stations and circuits
events.description: Joshua Woodlin, District Book Steward: the Philadelphia Annual Conference had moved a committee of three to apportion the Bishop's allowance but none was appointed; after interviewing Bishop Willis Nazrey (arrived with family to preside over the Philadelphia and New England Districts; address 606 Pine Street, above Sixth) he divides the sum by membership, requiring Philadelphia District members to pay 'a little over seven cents apiece'. Apportionment as printed: 1 Bethel Church, Phila., $100.00; 2 Union Church, Phila., $30.00; 3 Wesley Church, Phila., $15.00; 4 Zion City Mission, Phila., $10.00; 5 Camden, N.J., $10.00; 6 Frankford Circuit $20.00; 7 Bucks County Circuit $15.00; 8 Bordentown Circuit $20.00; 9 Trenton Circuit $20.00; 10 Bridgeton Circuit $25.00; 11 West Chester $2?.00 [amount illegible]; 12 Princeton Circuit $15.00; 13 Freehold Circuit $15.00; 14 Reading Circuit $20.00; 15 Norristown Circuit $20.00; 16 New Brunswick Circuit $15.00; 17 Burlington Circuit $27.50; 18 Penningtonville Circuit $20.00; 19 Salem Circuit $27.00; 20 Cape May Circuit $15.00; 21 Lancaster Circuit $20.00; 22 Denville [sic] Circuit $15.00.

events.name: Goines vs. McCandless: community committee, subscriptions and planned appeal
events.description: Correspondent (signature illegible), replying to 'W. S.' (26 Jan): the suit was not sought by Mr. Goines but arose from his ejection; meetings were called to raise money; a committee managed it; petitions had been sent to the railway company 'on more than one occasion' and were met with silent contempt; counsel were W. S. Peirce [VERIFY], Esq., and ex-Supreme Court judge Mr. Knox; the case is to be taken to the Supreme Court and further meetings will be called to raise funds. Dated Phila., Jan. 28th, 1861.

events.name: Rev. John Cornish's quarterly meetings, Old Chester and New Chester
events.description: Notice: Rev. John Cornish's Quarterly Meeting at Old Chester on the 17th inst. (1861-02-17) and at New Chester on the 24th (1861-02-24). (Same notice announces Rev. L. C. Speaks' quarterly meeting, Saturday and Sabbath evenings 9th-10th inst.; Speaks is elder of Bridge Street Church, Brooklyn, per the same page, so not linked.)

events.name: Ladies of the John Cornish Society -- anniversary
events.description: The ladies of the John Cornish Society held their anniversary on 'Wednesday evening, the 10th inst.' (date as printed is inconsistent: 10 Feb 1861 was a Sunday and postdates the 9 Feb issue). Mrs. Carter, President; assisted by Mrs. Harris; Annual Report read by Mrs. Seymour. The society had on hand about $1,860 [VERIFY third digit; could be $1,560]. A number of ministers were invited to partake of the refreshments. Location not stated (presumably Philadelphia). Compare CR_1861-02-23 p3 standing notice of 'The Daughters of Cornish Society', Mrs. Sarah Carter, President.

events.name: Donation visit to Rev. J. P. Campbell, Trenton A.M.E. Church
events.description: Members of the A.M.E. Church, Trenton, N.J., paid their pastor Rev. J. P. Campbell a donation visit on Tuesday the 5th inst.; some $17 cash and about $20 in presents [VERIFY both amounts; faint].

events.name: Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity -- grand demonstration
events.description: Grand demonstration of the entire Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity at Bethel Church, Thursday evening Feb. 7, 1861; officers and members of the grand and subordinate tabernacles, in and out of the State, to meet in the basement. By order of Rev. Stephen Smith, Grand Worthy Superior; second signer (Grand Scribe) illegible. Reported in CR_1861-02-16 p2: addresses by Rev. S. Smith, Mr. A. M. Green, Rev. Wm. Douglass.

events.name: Lecture for the benefit of Union Baptist Church
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Little Pine Street above Sixth, Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. J. W[heaton?] Smith [VERIFY name; probably the white Baptist minister Rev. J. Wheaton Smith, so not linked] lectures at the Union Baptist church, Little Pine Street above Sixth, Tuesday the 12th at 8 p.m., on 'The Discoveries made by him in the Holy Land: Hill of Calvary, the Mount of Olives', etc. Tickets [15 cents? VERIFY] at [one outlet illegible], Rev. E. Weaver's Book Concern, Pine Street above Sixth; Rev. J. Asher, Rodman Street above Tenth; Rev. J. Nickens, No. 1029 [VERIFY] Rodman Street; the Masonic Hall, Eleventh Street; or at the door. Proceeds to assist the Church in paying a very pressing debt. Brothers Shadd, Lively, Burrows, Johnson and others expected to assist the Choir.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's episcopal appointments, Philadelphia Conference circuits
events.description: Episcopal visitation schedule signed W. Nazrey: Bordentown circuit, N.J., Mar 1-8; Princeton Mar 8-11; Brunswick Mar 11-15; Burlington Mar 15-21; West Chester Mar 23-30; Penningtonville Mar 30-Apr 5; Columbia Apr 6-13. Ministers of the circuits to arrange preaching points. Repeated CR_1861-02-16 p3 and 02-23 p3.

events.name: Rev. S. Smith's Mission Church -- quarterly meeting
events.location: Rev. S. Smith's Mission Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Editor attended Rev. S. Smith's Mission Church Quarterly Meeting 'on the 13th ult.'; a very interesting occasion; a protracted meeting was announced to continue. (Probably Rev. Stephen Smith; identification not stated.)

events.name: Editor Weaver's visit to West Chester
events.description: Editor (Weaver) preached at West Chester on Monday night Feb. 11 with Rev. R. Barney, pastor in charge; church three quarters of a mile out of town; house well filled despite rain; sold papers and obtained some ten cash subscribers. Mrs. Jane Thomas and Miss Ruth Anna Johnson each paid $1.00; other names to appear hereafter. (Announced CR_1861-02-09 p3.)

events.name: Philadelphia Library Company -- lecture on 'Books' and debate
events.location: Lecture-room, St. Thomas' Episcopal Church, South Fifth Street below Walnut, Philadelphia
events.description: Prof. J. P. Leslie [VERIFY spelling] of the American Philosophical Society lectured on 'Books' (arranging a library by the seven prismatic colors). A debate ensued between Messrs. Isaiah C. Wear [VERIFY], John C. B[...] and Wm. W[...] [surnames largely illegible; possibly Bowers and Whipper, not confirmed] on the question 'Could the Colored People, by taking active part in the present ... [illegible]'; Mr. Wear in the affirmative, the other two in the negative. Held in the lecture-room of St. Thomas' Episcopal Church, South Fifth street below Walnut.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's visit to Trenton, N.J.
events.description: Bishop Nazrey and lady arrived at Trenton Saturday (Feb. 9) at 1 p.m.; Sabbath (Feb. 10) at 11 a.m. preached on 2 Tim. iii. 11; also addressed the Sabbath school connected with the church and preached again. Reported by J. P. Campbell, Trenton, Feb. 11, 1861.

events.name: Banneker Institute -- lecture by Professor A. M. Green
events.description: On 'Tuesday evening' (computed as 1861-02-19, the Tuesday before the issue [VERIFY]) Professor A. M. Green [VERIFY] lectured before the Banneker Institute on reminiscences of the anti-slavery movement and the duty of the colored people during the crisis; audience small at first, respectable by the close; frequently applauded. Afterward Mr. D. D. Turner read an article from the Sunday Dispatch (of the 10th inst.) on citizenship and the right of petition, written by a member of the Institute in reply to an item of the 3d inst. denying the right of colored persons to petition.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey at Pennington and Trenton, N.J.
events.description: Bishop Nazrey, his lady and the writer drove to Pennington on the Sabbath (computed 1861-02-17, the Sabbath after the Feb. 10 Trenton visit [VERIFY]); arrived a few minutes before twelve; Bishop preached on Heb. iv. 11 ('Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest'), then addressed the congregation on the condition of our people; first episcopal visit there since about six years before. In the evening he preached at Trenton to a full house on Heb. xi. 16 ('But now they desire a better country'). Notes the Recorder taking hold; 25 copies wanted instead of 10.

events.name: Publication Society -- meeting called at Bethel Church
events.description: Members of the Publication Society requested to meet 'next Thursday evening' (computed 1861-02-28) in Bethel Church at half-past seven, business of importance. By order of the President, Mrs. Laws [printed thus; same society's president read 'Mrs. Laws' in CR_1861-01-19].

events.name: Itinerant Preachers' Aid Society of the Philadelphia Conference -- meeting
events.location: Study of Bethel Church, Sixth Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Members of the Itinerant Preachers' Aid Society of the Philadelphia Conference, A.M.E. Church, notified to meet Tuesday Feb. 26, 1861, 10 a.m., study of Bethel Church, Sixth Street; [middle line partly illegible: 'The Executive ... is requested']. By order of the President. Richard Robinson, President; Joshua Woodlin, Sec'y. (Same notice in CR_1861-02-16 p3, nearly illegible there.)

events.name: Grand Tabernacle, Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity -- meeting
events.location: Ma[sonic?] Hall, 11th Street near Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: A meeting of the Grand Tabernacle of the Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity will be held Friday, 1st of March, at Ma[sonic?] Hall, 11th Street near Pine, at 7 1/2 o'clock, by order of [name illegible], G. W. Superior; attest J. W[...] [illegible], Secretary.

events.name: Henry Davis Society -- meeting with invited clergy
events.description: Meeting of the Henry Davis Society on Tuesday night, 26 Feb. 1861, at the Philadelphia Institute. The editor (Elisha Weaver) attended on an invitation delivered by 'brother Seymour' from the President and members; he had not known the society existed. A number of clergymen were invited, shared a 'free-will offering' (refreshments), and all the ministers gave addresses, after which the society voted them thanks. The society 'has upwards of $600 in the treasury.' Editor asks all societies to place a card for one year 'like the Daughters of Cornish.' President not named.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's week on the Trenton Circuit
events.location: Trenton, Pennington and New Hope (Trenton Circuit, N.J.)
events.description: Bishop W. Nazrey left Philadelphia 9 Feb. 1861 [VERIFY day] for Trenton, met by Brother Campbell; Sister Campbell ill. Spent a week on the Trenton Circuit, which he had travelled in 1842. Trenton congregation has built 'a very beautiful little church' under Elder Campbell, with a fine Sabbath school; visited Pennington ('a neat little church'); went to New Hope to see relations; left 21st ult. (21 Feb.) for Philadelphia.

events.name: ICY winter lecture course -- Douglass on Elocution
events.location: High School rooms, Lombard Street above 7th, Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. Wm. Douglass, Rector of St. Thomas' (Episcopal) Church, 'gave an eloquent discourse on Elocution, which was well attended and received' on the evening of the 15th instant (February). Part of the annual winter course given by colored men at the Institute for Colored Youth, broadened this season from physical sciences to literary subjects.
attendees: lecturer; Rector, St. Thomas' Episcopal Church (Rev.)

events.name: ICY winter lecture course -- Catto on Language
events.location: High School rooms, Lombard Street above 7th, Philadelphia
events.description: 'On last Thursday evening, 22d instant, Mr. Octavius V. Catto, a graduate of the High School, and at present a worthy and efficient teacher therein, delivered one on Language, which was quite scholarly and acceptable. It was well attended.' Note: 22 Feb. 1861 was a Friday; the paper says Thursday [VERIFY date].
attendees: lecturer; ICY graduate and teacher (middle initial faint)

events.name: Publication Society -- members called to meet at Bethel Church
events.description: Notice (very faint print) calling all members of the Publication Society to meet 'on next [weekday illegible] evening, in Bethel Church, without fail, at half past seven o'clock. Business of importance.' Signed by order of the President, 'Mrs. Laws' (January notice spelled Mrs. Laws). Day of meeting unreadable, so no date given.

events.name: Zion Mission Sabbath School -- anniversary
events.location: Zion Mission, Seventh St. below Dickerson St., Philadelphia
events.description: Anniversary of the Zion Mission Sabbath School, Thursday 7 March 1861 at 7 1/2 P.M. The Mission is 'under the pastoral charge of Rev. S. Smith, Superintendent, and Rev. Thos. Jones, of Sabbath School' (the printed sentence is ambiguous about which man holds which office; last line faint).

events.name: Bishop Nazrey visits Bethel Church Sabbath School
events.description: Bishop Willis Nazrey visited the Sabbath School of Bethel Church on Sunday 24 Feb. 1861. He recalls first visiting it in 1842; was stationed over the Bethel congregation in 1846 (two years) and again in 1851 (one year, until appointed elsewhere by the General Conference); gave the city's Sabbath schools an Annual Conference address in 1856 and was then absent about five years. The school numbered 650 scholars in 1856 and 'is now very large'; he recommends its system of instruction to all schools. Teachers not named.
attendees: bishop, visitor (signer); former pastor of Bethel 1846-48, 1851

events.name: Trenton Circuit report
events.description: Letter of J. P. Campbell dated Trenton, N.J., Feb. 25, 1861. Three appointments on the Trenton Circuit. The Trenton house, 'upon one of the most beautiful streets' in a wealthy neighbourhood, was rebuilt and remodelled at about $2,000 under Rev. C. Woodyard some two years ago; remaining debt not over $280. The house at Pennington is free from debt (all claims paid within four months). At 'Louisville' [sic; place uncertain] a band of men and women meet in private houses and support the gospel liberally. Campbell carries copies of the Recorder on pastoral visits for sale and urges support of both the Recorder and the Repository.

events.name: Revivals on the Penningtonville Circuit and at Frankford
events.location: Penningtonville, Coleraine and Britain (Pa.); Frankford, Pa.
events.description: Brother I. J. Hill of Penningtonville Circuit reports a series of meetings with about fifteen conversions at Penningtonville and sixteen at Coleraine; writing from Britain [Britain Township?] he is holding a protracted meeting with mourners crowding the altar. 'Rev. R. Robertson, at Frankford, Pa., has just closed his Protracted Meetings, after some two or three weeks' labor'; old citizens say they never saw such a work in Frankford before.

events.name: Banneker Institute -- Gibbs lecture and Haytian emigration debate
events.description: On a Tuesday evening (probably 5 March 1861; 'Tuesday evening' only) Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs lectured on Religious Intolerance (about twenty minutes). A debate followed on 'Should the colored people emigrate to Hayti?' Affirmative: A. M. Green and I. W. (I. Wesley) Simpson. Negative: D. B. Bawser, J. C. (John C.) Bowers and Mr. Powell. Mr. Powell, 'a resident of England, and an officer under the government--though a colored man--was once a resident of Philadelphia,' was recognised by former associates and remarked on the great changes since he left.

events.name: Corner-stone laying, Mount Moriah A.M.E. Church
events.description: Corner stone of the A.M.E. Mount Moriah Church to be laid 16 March 1861 at 3 P.M., with a special collection for the building. Notice signed Henry Davis, Minister, dated March 2, 1861 (first printed, illegibly, in CR_1861-03-02 p3; text read on the 03-09 reprint).

events.name: Daughters of Cornish Society -- standing card
events.description: Card of the Daughters of Cornish Society (first in CR_1861-03-02 p3; repeated 03-09 and 03-16): stated quarterly meetings on the first Wednesdays of February, May, August and November; Board meets the Wednesday before each. Officers: Mrs. Sarah Carter, President; Mrs. L. B. Seymour, Sec'y (printed 'Mr. I. B. ...' in 03-09, 'Mrs. L. B. Seymour' or 'I. B.' in 03-16). The 03-02 editorial on the Henry Davis Society praises the Daughters of Cornish for buying a year's card.

events.name: Daughters of the Rush Society -- anniversary
events.description: The Daughters of the Rush Society held their 'first anniversary' on Wednesday the 12th inst. (12 March 1861 was a Tuesday [VERIFY]). The society is 33 years old (founded c. 1828) and 'said to be the oldest in the city.' The Secretary's address (Secretary not named) reported $12,000 raised and distributed in sick and burial aid, with some $1,587.82 in the treasury. Clergy invited to address the meeting; refreshments served by the ladies. Editor remarks that the colored people of Philadelphia have more society money in the Saving Banks than any other class. No officers named.

events.name: ICY winter lecture course -- Gibbs on Geology
events.location: High School Rooms, Nos. 716 and 718 Lombard Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Seventh lecture of the course, Thursday 7 March 1861: Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs, A.M. (Dartmouth College; Princeton Theological Seminary; pastor of the First Presbyterian Church, Seventh Street below Shippen) on Geology, to a good audience; editor demurs at the recession of Niagara Falls and boulders boring into rock. Announced: eighth lecture by Prof. Robert Campbell, formerly a teacher in the High School, more recently of the Niger Valley Exploring Expedition; then S. M. Douglass; and, it is hoped, 'brother W[surname illegible], of Bethel Church, whom, we understand, Prof. Bassett has especially invited.' Lectures free to all; each lecturer receives a small fee from the Institute.

events.name: Grand United Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity -- officers' disavowal
events.description: Letter dated March 11th [VERIFY], 1861, signed G. W. Harman, G. W. S.; E. W. Hemmenway, G. W. N. S.; E. F. Nixon, P. G. W. U. S.; John H. Hughes, G. G. D. M. They reply to an obituary by 'H. G. R.' (CR 23 Feb. 1861) of Sister Anna B. Bedford (spelled Belford/Bedford), formerly Anna B. Powell, 'considered the mother of the Order.' They state there are two orders of Love and Charity: the 'Grand United Order', the elder, and the 'Independent Order' to which Anna Bedford belonged at her death; she had not been a member of the United Order for upwards of four or five years, having broken fellowship with 'her sister Ruth, and her brother, M. A. M.' Members of the United Order nevertheless attended her funeral.
attendees: officer, G. W. S.; [VERIFY name reading]
officer, G. W. N. S.; [VERIFY name reading]
officer, P. G. W. U. S. [VERIFY]; [VERIFY name reading]

events.name: Meeting in aid of Rev. Andrew Wheeler's family (collection for redemption from slavery)
events.location: Rev. Mr. Willson's church, Philadelphia [VERIFY spelling of Willson; church not otherwise identified]
events.description: Reprinted letter (Christian Instructor) signed F. C., dated Philadelphia, March 12th, 1861: 'I was present at a meeting, last evening, in Rev. Mr. Willson's church, when a small collection was taken up', for the Rev. Andrew Wheeler (Methodist minister), recently manumitted under the will of his late owner, a lady in Maryland, whose wife belongs to a person residing in Baltimore. The claimant offers to sell the wife for $250, the eldest child 'Henrietta,' aged six, for $350, Thomas, aged four, for $300, the baby 'Frank' thrown in with the mother: $900 in all. Wheeler is a Maryland minister visiting Philadelphia, so he is not linked; the Philadelphia church is identified only as 'Rev. Mr. Willson's church'.

events.name: Publication Society of Philadelphia -- committee presents $10 to the Christian Recorder
events.description: The Publication Society of Philadelphia (the women's society that aids the paper; its president was reported as Mrs. Laws in CR_1861-01-19) sent a committee to wait on the editor, Rev. Elisha Weaver, and present $10.00. Committee as printed: 'Rev. Mrs. Mary Frisby, Mrs. Mary Bell, and Mrs. Mary Jones'. The same editorial lists ministers elsewhere who most support the Book Concern (Rev. Messrs. Moore, Weir, Crippen and Watson of the New York Conference; Geo. A. Rue and H. J. Young of New England; W. H. Waters and Daniel W. Moore of Baltimore; G. H. Graham and Daniel Cooper of Ohio; not linked) and says the Philadelphia Conference members 'all, as a general thing, came up square to the work'. Date of the presentation not stated (before March 23).

events.name: Rev. John Cornish's quarterly meetings (West Philadelphia, Germantown, Norristown, Chester circuits)
events.location: West Chester [VERIFY], West Philadelphia, Norristown, Chester, Germantown, Horntown [VERIFY]
events.description: Schedule as printed: 'Tea Chester' [sic; probably West Chester] March 31st; West Philadelphia April 7th; Norristown April 14th; Chester April 20th; Germantown April 28th; 'Horntown' [VERIFY reading] May 5th, 1861. One event for the series; first date given.

events.name: Rev. Peter Gardiner's fourth quarterly meetings (Salem / Woodbury NJ circuits)
events.location: Salem, Frogtown, Bushtown, Dutchtown, Woodbury, N.J.
events.description: Signed notice of Peter Gardiner: fourth quarterly meetings at Salem April 7th; Frogtown April 14th; Bushtown April 21st; Dutchtown May 5th; Woodbury May 12th (1861). NJ circuits of the Philadelphia Conference.

events.name: Dr. H. J. Brown's lectures on phrenology, physiology and the laws of health
events.description: Report 'For the Recorder': Dr. H. J. Brown of Burlington, New Jersey, 'paid us a visit a few days ago' and gave two lectures on phrenology, physiology and the laws of health. Last summer he visited the principal cities of the Eastern States; the writer urges him to lecture also in remote localities in New Jersey. The end of the piece (top of col. 2) is lost in a tear in the film; a fragment there ends 'Allentown, March [..], 1861', so the writer may be at Allentown, N.J. [VERIFY]. Place of the lectures not stated.

events.name: Funeral of James Prosser
events.description: Domestic News item: James Prosser, who for nearly half a century kept a restaurant in Market street, Philadelphia, 'favorably known to the greater portion of the business community', compared with Downing of New York (George T. Downing, presumably); left about $2?,000 [figure partly illegible]. A partly illegible line appears to say his funeral was 'Saturday last' [VERIFY], i.e. about 1861-03-16. 'He would, at any time, sooner have gone to the poor house than tell a lie.'

events.name: Hutchinson Family concert for the Social, Civil and Statistical Association of Colored People of Pennsylvania
events.description: The Association ('a Society of a high literary character of this city') engaged the Hutchinson family (five in number) for a concert at Sansom Street Hall. The hall was 'crowded to its utmost capacity with white and colored folks'; many stood. The editor attended. The Family invited 'our noted and distinguished friend and Professor, Mr. Bowers' onto the platform twice to perform with them. Announced in CR_1861-03-23 p2 (faded notice). No officers of the Association named.
attendees: editor, attended as guest (Rev.) [inferred from editorial 'we']

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's visitation of the New Jersey circuits
events.location: Bordentown, Allentown, Princeton, New Brunswick, Burlington, Mount Holly, N.J.
events.description: Bishop W. Nazrey's account: arrived Bordentown circuit about 10 o'clock Saturday, preached Sabbath morning and evening; the church 'not as prosperous as some years ago', no local preachers and the circuit preacher there only once in four weeks. Monday to Allentown: church had upwards of 100 members in 1844, now only some 30 or 40; Brother Francis Raynor took the Bishop to his house (rents a farm of some 150 acres at $800 per annum, paid for the last eight years). Next to Princeton (preached Sabbath; new house of worship in course of erection), then Brunswick until Friday (large church building under erection); both places anxious to keep their present ministers another year. Friday to Burlington (preached that evening); next morning to Mount Holly where 'at 3 [VERIFY] o'clock in the afternoon we laid the corner-stone for a new church'. Henry Davis's letter (same page) dates the Burlington sermon to 15 March and places the 16 March cornerstone at Clarksborough [discrepancy; see flags].

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth winter lecture: Mrs. S. M. Douglass on the circulation of the blood
events.description: Mrs. S. M. Douglass lectured on the circulation of blood in creative beings and of fluid in plants, birds and reptiles, to a crowded house; 'Mrs. D. is noted as an extraordinary lecturer.' The winter lectures are nearly over for the season; the first was given by Prof. Bassett, Principal of the school. The editor praises the Institute's teachers and asks why the Board of Managers (Controllers) of this city do not employ colored teachers in public schools where the children are all colored, 'for instance, Sixth Street Colored School, where some eight or ten teachers are required.'

events.name: Rev. Spencer Logan's quarterly meetings (Bucks County circuit)
events.location: New Hope, Buckingham Mountains, Newtown, Attleborough, Pa.
events.description: Signed Spencer Logan, dated Philadelphia, March 2? [VERIFY], 1861: quarterly meetings at New Hope April 21st; Buckingham Mountains April 28th; Newtown May 5th; Attleborough May 12th.

events.name: Bishop Nazrey's episcopal visit to the Burlington circuit (cornerstone laid)
events.location: Burlington circuit, N.J.: Burlington, Clarksborough, Mount Moriah (near Mount Holly), Evesham Mount, Milford, Snowhill, Jordantown
events.description: Henry Davis, minister in charge of the Burlington circuit, dated March 21, 1861: Bishop Nazrey and his wife arrived 15 March about noon; he preached at Burlington that evening (Psalm 1:3). 16 March at Clarksborough, a corner stone for a new church was laid by the Bishop and the minister in charge of the Burlington circuit (Isaiah 28:16). 17 March, 10 o'clock, Mount Moriah church near Mount Holly (Song of Solomon 2:3); evening 7 1/2 o'clock, Evesham Mount church (Colossians 3:1). 18 March, Milford church, 7 1/2 o'clock (Luke 16:2). 19 March, Snowhill church (Psalm 24:12-13 as printed). 20 March, A. M. E. Union Bethel church, Jordantown (Acts 2:44), closing the visit. Large congregations at each appointment.
attendees: minister in charge of the Burlington circuit, letter-writer

events.name: Independent Order of Brothers and Sisters of Love and Charity -- tribute to deceased sister Anna B. Bedford
events.description: Letter of Nathaniel Wiggins, Grand Scribe, I. O. B. and S. of L. and C., answering the March 16th notice signed G. W. S., G. W. N. S., P. G. W. U. S., G. G. D. M. (and an earlier article signed 'H. G. B.', later printed 'H. G. R.' [VERIFY]) about the death and funeral of Anna B. Bedford. Few attended her funeral because no notice of her death reached the Order except her own number; her brother testified to a neglect by the Scribe of No. 1, to which she belonged; members visited her in her sickness. Anna had earlier left 'her sister Ruth, her brother M. A. M. [VERIFY initials]' (i.e., another body) to join the Independent Order. 'Every subordinate tabernacle in the compact in the city, including the grand Tabernacle and Encampment, have paid a tribute of the highest regard known to the Order to our deceased sister.'
attendees: Grand Scribe, I. O. B. and S. of L. and C.

events.name: Bishop Willis Nazrey's proposed episcopal visits (Frankford, Salem, Greenwich, Reading circuits)
events.description: Signed Willis Nazrey: Frankford circuit April 13th; Salem circuit April 20th; Greenwich circuit April 27th; Reading circuit May 4th (1861); subject to change.
